title: What are the tops of these three row pyramids?
description: The tops of three pyramids with three rows are found without building them, using the rule eigh plus two bee plus see from the solved example. The bottom rows are four, thirteen and eight, then seven, eleven and three, then ten, fourteen and twenty five.
teaching_notes: One idea: the top of a three row pyramid is the two end numbers once each plus the middle number twice. Watch for students who add the three bottom numbers once each.

video_script.why: The child finds the top of three pyramids from their bottom rows without building them, as the solved example did with letters.
video_script.substitution: Put the end numbers once and the middle number twice into eigh plus two bee plus see.
video_script.anchor: three bottom row cards, 4 13 8 and 7 11 3 and 10 14 25
video_script.payoff_line: The tops are thirty eight, thirty two and sixty three.

final_answer.spoken: the tops are thirty eight, thirty two and sixty three

video_script.design: One idea: end numbers once, middle number twice. The three bottom row cards stay in the anchor band and each sum sits on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the top of each pyramid.
<bookmark mark='put'/>Step one, for four, thirteen and eight, the middle number thirteen is counted twice. Two times thirteen is twenty six.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Four plus twenty six plus eight is thirty eight.
<bookmark mark='put'/>Step two, for seven, eleven and three, two times eleven is twenty two.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Seven plus twenty two plus three is thirty two.
<bookmark mark='put'/>Step three, for ten, fourteen and twenty five, two times fourteen is twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Ten plus twenty eight plus twenty five is sixty three.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The tops are thirty eight, thirty two and sixty three.
